 LEE COUNTY, Fla. (WINK) — The School District of Lee County is recommending closing Orangewood Elementary School and Tice Elementary School at the end of the 2026-2027 school year.
 Letters to both school communities said an analysis of district enrollment and facility needs showed each school faced decreasing enrollment and high operating costs. The district said the proposed closures were part of a long-term plan to support student success across the community.
 “We know this proposal brings up strong emotions, questions, and concerns,” the School District of Lee County said.
 The district said Orangewood Elementary has a 77-year history and Tice Elementary has a 99-year history. It said recommendations like this are never made lightly.
 On Wednesday, Tice Elementary received three school grants from the Foundation for Lee County Public Schools. 
 The School Board of Lee County will vote on the recommendation at its December 8, 2026 meeting. If the board approves it, district staff will work with families on preferential placement of their children in a school.
 Former Lee County School Board member Gwynetta Gittens said she wanted the district to consider a different approach. “Maybe combine the two schools to one something. But no one is going to have any opportunity until after they voted on what they're going to do. So I understand about the low numbers and all of that, but we've got to get a little more creative. We really do as to how to handle these budget cuts,” Gittens said.
 The district scheduled a parent meeting for Orangewood Elementary families at 5:30 p.m. on Tuesday, December 1 at the school. It scheduled a parent meeting for Tice Elementary families at 5:30 p.m. on Wednesday, December 2 at the school.
 The letters thanked families and the community for their partnership, dedication and support of students and each school community. The December vote will decide whether both schools close at the end of the 2026-2027 school year.
